summary.headline: Cochin Shipyard Q1 FY27 PAT fell to INR 151.45 crore from INR 187.82 crore on turnover of INR 1,094.21 crore; ISRF JV with DP World's Drydocks World valued at INR 1,800 crore.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 turnover rose about 2.4% YoY to INR 1,094.21 crore, but PBT fell to INR 202.49 crore from INR 249.54 crore and PAT to INR 151.45 crore from INR 187.82 crore. Management cited EBITDA margin around 24% and PAT margin around 14% for the quarter. The company delivered three vessels in the period, plus three by subsidiary Udupi Cochin Shipyard. Management announced several strategic moves: a 50:50 JV with Drydocks World for the ISRF ship repair facility, a scaled-down block fabrication plan after HD KSOE talks failed, a Tuticorin hybrid yard lease, and a Green Maritime battery JV.

segments.name: Shipbuilding
segments.commentary: Management said shipbuilding is about 70% of turnover at 10-12% EBITDA margin. Deliveries in FY27 so far include the third of eight ASW shallow water crafts, a second multipurpose vessel for a German client, and a Ro-Ro ferry for Kochi Municipal Corporation.

segments.name: Ship repair
segments.commentary: Ship repair is about 30% of turnover at roughly 20-24% EBITDA margin. ISRF has a 6,000-ton ship lift, about 1,400 m berthing and annual capacity of up to 82 ships.

segments.name: Udupi Cochin Shipyard (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Delivered three vessels in the period: two 3,800 TDW general cargo vessels to Wilson Group, Norway, and a 70-tonne bollard pull tug to Polestar Maritime (Adani Group). Management said land constraints limit its new order intake.

segments.name: Green Maritime battery JV (with HBL, 40% CSL)
segments.commentary: Incorporated June 2026 for marinized energy storage systems. Target revenue INR 640 crore by year 5 and about 20% EBITDA margin (ballpark, business plan not final). Total capital INR 50 crore; no manufacturing facility, as HBL will manufacture.

guidance_outlook: Turnover growth guidance of about 12% per year, with management saying it could reach 12-15%.
Blended EBITDA margin guided at around 14-15% for the year on a conservative basis, down from prior years' higher margins.

Target to deliver about 10 vessels in FY27 (three delivered so far in Q1): two more ASWs by December 2026, two more multipurpose vessels, a trailing suction hopper dredger next month, and commissioning service vessels and Samskip container vessels through early 2027.
Operating cash flow expected to turn positive in FY27 as delivery-linked milestone payments come in.
ISRF JV transaction targeted for completion before end of FY27, subject to Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, DIPAM, and CSL shareholder (postal ballot) approvals.
New investments targeted at a return on capital of about 14-15%.
capex_capacity: ISRF JV: INR 1,800 crore slump-sale consideration, 50% in cash and 50% in JV equity. Expected revenue about INR 600 crore over the next 2 years, scaling to INR 1,000-1,200 crore over 5 years. Plan adds 10 workstations.

Block fabrication: Earlier 1 lakh tonne plan with HD KSOE is now a solo facility of about 60,000 tonnes per annum. Current capacity is about 12,000 tonnes per annum, for total throughput near 72,000 tonnes.

Vadinar (Gujarat) ship repair with Deendayal Port Authority: two floating drydocks for ~250 m vessels. CCEA approval received May 2026. Environmental clearance expected shortly; operations targeted within 36 months of EC. Revenue about INR 300-600 crore after 3 years.

Tuticorin (V.O. Chidambaranar Port): won 30-year lease at one-time payment of INR 305.76 crore for about 110 acres land and 17.29 acres waterfront. In DPR stage; revenue of INR 650-700 crore initially, scaling to INR 1,800-2,000 crore over 7-8 years.

Total capex over about 5 years estimated by an analyst at INR 6,000-6,500 crore across the four projects. Funding targeted at about 80:20 debt-equity. Applied for Shipbuilding Development Scheme (25% capex subsidy) and MDF Interest Incentivisation Fund (up to 3% interest subvention).
demand_pricing: Defence pipeline per management: LPD (4 numbers, about INR 32,000 crore), MCMV (12 numbers, about INR 36,000 crore), P-17 Bravo (7 numbers, about INR 49,000 crore). Management said these are RFPs with competition; LPD and MCMV seen as more suitable than P-17 Bravo.
NGSV: CSL is L1 for five next-generation survey vessels worth about INR 5,000 crore; order signing expected around November 2026. Navy procedures are slow (CCS and PNC approvals).

Commercial: Dredging Corporation of India sister dredger (about INR 1,300 crore, nomination basis) expected within about two months. Andaman 4 x 500-passenger vessels under nomination discussion. Government demand aggregation for about 432 vessels over 10 years, with SCI/BCSL tenders in progress. MR tanker technical bid indicative cost about INR 1,700 crore; Aframax EOI indicative cost about INR 2,600 crore.
Export: European commercial vessels from 2023-24 orders are 80-90% complete but only about 30% paid; payment is tail-ended (around 70% on delivery).
Management said the Green Tug Transition Program could create about INR 1,000 crore of battery-led investment over 10 years, with real volume expected in 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Green Maritime battery JV: product basket, 3-year scale, and timing of meaningful contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Target product range is marine energy storage and power management systems, with revenue target of INR 640 crore by year 5. Management said the JV will not contribute much revenue immediately; it has placed an order for the battery systems for four green tugs being built, and the JV's turnover will be battery-system only, not the tug. Total capital is INR 50 crore, with no manufacturing facility; HBL manufactures.

qa_highlights.question: ISRF JV with Drydocks World: will it serve DP World vessels only, and how is overlap with CSL's business handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CSL will take orders and the JV will execute them, with DDW free to bring in its own clients. Management said the ISRF only handles vessels up to 130 m and 6,000 tonnes, larger vessels go to the main yard, and the two parties have a clear understanding that DDW will not enter CSL's other segments.

qa_highlights.question: Defence and commercial order pipeline and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Defence RFPs: LPD 4 numbers (about INR 32,000 crore), MCMV 12 numbers (about INR 36,000 crore), P-17 Bravo 7 numbers (about INR 49,000 crore). NGSV contract expected around November 2026. DCI sister dredger (about INR 1,300 crore, nomination) expected within about two months. Demand aggregation of 432 vessels over 10 years is in tender stage.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 operating cash flow negative, and what are the normalised cash conversion and ROC targets?
qa_highlights.answer: European export contracts are tail-ended: about 30% received against 80-90% construction completion, with 70% due on delivery. Management expects operating cash flow to turn positive in FY27 as deliveries come in, and targets a return on new investments of about 14-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Why are EBITDA margins falling from the past three years, and how should the 14% full-year guide be read against a Q1 margin above 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Past higher margins came from nominated orders (indigenous aircraft carrier, two aircraft carrier refits) and interest income on a cash surplus of INR 2,000-3,000 crore that has been used for ISRF and drydock capex, so is no longer available. Shipbuilding runs at 10-12% EBITDA margin (about 70% of turnover) and ship repair at 20-24% (about 30%), giving a blended 14-15% on a conservative basis. Management said EBITDA includes interest income as a recurring item.

qa_highlights.question: Vessel delivery schedule for FY27 and the capex revenue potential for the four new projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is about 10 deliveries in FY27, with three done. Two more ASWs by December 2026, two more MPVs, a trailing suction hopper dredger next month, two Cyprus commissioning service vessels (October 2026 and around February/March 2027), and one Samskip container vessel by February. ISRF revenue of about INR 600 crore over 2 years, rising to INR 1,000-1,200 crore over 5 years. Vadinar about INR 300 crore after 36 months from EC. Tuticorin INR 650-700 crore initially, scaling to INR 1,800-2,000 crore over 7-8 years. Funding around 80:20 debt-equity, with 25% capex subsidy and 3% interest subvention applied for.

risks_watch: Full-year EBITDA margin guide of 14-15% sits well below prior years; loss of nominated, high-margin defence and refit work and of interest income from the cash surplus are the drivers.

Operating cash flow was negative in FY26 and is expected to turn positive only in FY27, dependent on about 7 vessels of delivery-linked milestone payments (around 70% of contract value) from European export orders that are about 30% paid.

Order inflow depends on RFPs and tenders with uncertain timing: NGSV (about INR 5,000 crore, expected around November 2026), DCI dredger (about INR 1,300 crore), and MR and Aframax tenders. Management declined to give a timeline for LPD, MCMV and P-17 Bravo.
ISRF JV needs MoPSW, DIPAM and CSL postal-ballot approvals before completion, targeted before end FY27. Watch for the postal ballot notice and EC for Vadinar.

Green Maritime JV economics are not final: the business plan is still being prepared, the 20% EBITDA margin is ballpark, and the JV's revenue is battery-only and largely unconsolidated (CSL holds 40%).

Capex of about INR 6,000-6,500 crore across four projects relies on subsidy and interest support; monitor debt levels, the 80:20 funding mix and execution of the block fabrication facility, now solo at about 60,000 tpa.
key_quotes: Since then, CSL and HD KSOE have had series of discussions and engagements. However, we have not been able to arrive at a mutually agreed definitive terms for establishing BF facility through a joint venture.

So, we have, between the 2 of us, have a very clear understanding that there will be no ingress into that market by DDW, and the current market share of CSL in the other segments will continue to be held by CSL.
So, blended will be around 14%, 15%, something like that on a very conservative basis.
But going forward, we cannot expect such margins from the commercial orders or the defense order, because now all the tenders from the defense is also on a tender basis.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the order pipeline, the ISRF JV and capex revenue targets, but cautious on margins and cash flow. It said the defence and commercial tenders are outside its control and gave no firm timelines, and it declined to give a firm margin for the Green Maritime JV or other ventures, calling the figures ballpark.

Block fabrication solo facility ~60,000 tpa (on top of ~12,000 tpa current capacity)
Vadinar two floating drydocks for ~250 m vessels (CCEA approved May 2026, EC pending)
Tuticorin hybrid yard (30-year lease, INR 305.76 cr upfront; DPR stage)

growth.why: Management guides ~12% annual turnover growth (possibly 12-15%), backed by ~INR 22,000 cr unexecuted order book (~27,000 cr post NGSV L1) and ~10 FY27 deliveries, but EBITDA margin guided down to ~14% and the new capacity (ISRF, 60k tpa block fabrication, Vadinar, Tuticorin) is 4+ quarters away or still in DPR/approval stage.
